analysis.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject. The לְ־ in לָרָקִיעַ marks the expanse as the thing God names, and שָׁמָיִם supplies the name he gives it.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־ and no suffix.

analysis.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject of the masculine singular verb וַיִּקְרָא, “he called.” The singular agreement identifies God as the one who named the expanse שָׁמָיִם, “heavens.”
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine plural absolute, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In וַיִּקְרָא אֱלֹהִים לָרָקִיעַ שָׁמָיִם, לָרָקִיעַ identifies the expanse that God names, and שָׁמָיִם gives it the name “heavens.”
analysis.morphology: Preposition לְ with the definite article, followed by a masculine singular absolute noun.

analysis.evidence: In וַיִּקְרָא אֱלֹהִים לָרָקִיעַ שָׁמָיִם, God gives the expanse (רָקִיעַ) the name שָׁמָיִם. The word therefore designates the sky.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine plural, absolute state, in pausal form.

analysis.evidence: The subject עֶרֶב follows וַיְהִי. The parallel clauses וַיְהִי עֶרֶב and וַיְהִי בֹקֶר narrate the arrival of evening and then morning on the second day.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־.

analysis.evidence: The paired clauses וַיְהִי עֶרֶב and וַיְהִי בֹקֶר describe evening followed by morning on the second day.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In וַיְהִי בֹקֶר, the masculine singular subject בֹקֶר follows the verb. The clause reports that morning came, parallel to the preceding וַיְהִי עֶרֶב, and repeats the wording of Genesis 1:5.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third-person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־

analysis.evidence: וַיְהִי בֹקֶר parallels וַיְהִי עֶרֶב. Evening and morning mark the second day.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute noun with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: After the evening and morning, שֵׁנִי ‘second’ modifies יוֹם and identifies the interval as the second day in the sequence.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In יוֹם שֵׁנִי, שֵׁנִי agrees with the masculine singular noun יוֹם and identifies the day as the second in the creation sequence.
